name: SPOSCOR Padel
author: powereight

sections.description:
SPOSCOR Padel is a dedicated padel plugin built on top of SPOSCOR Core. It adds padel-specific scoring — set by set, six games per set, two-game margin, with tie-break support — all designed to publish your match results quickly and beautifully.

Perfect for padel clubs, amateur pairs, local leagues, and tournament organizers who want a simple yet professional way to display match results on their WordPress site.

Why SPOSCOR Padel?

  • 5 minutes to publish. Just enter the set scores and paste a shortcode.
  • Set-by-set scoreboard. Games per set with tie-break decided sets (7-6).
  • Doubles-ready. Each side is a pair.
  • Mobile-first admin. Enter scores courtside on your phone, one-handed.
  • Beautiful display. Modern card design that looks great on any theme.

Features

  • Unlimited matches
  • Set-by-set scoreboard (best of 3, six games, two-game margin, tie-break)
  • 6 display themes (Light / Dark / Mono / Pro / Studio / Minimal)
  • Multilingual: English, Japanese, Spanish

Pro Features ($39/year)

  • Unlimited tournaments (leagues & knockout brackets)
  • Standings tables
  • Full design customization (colors & sizes)
  • OBS streaming view for live broadcasts
  • Priority support

Requires SPOSCOR Core

This plugin needs the free “SPOSCOR Core” plugin to work. Install and activate SPOSCOR Core first.

Pricing

SPOSCOR Padel comes in two plans: a free version (everything above) and Pro at $39/year, which adds unlimited tournaments, standings tables, full design customization, and OBS streaming.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the free “SPOSCOR Core” plugin.
  2. Upload the SPOSCOR Padel plugin to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  3. Activate SPOSCOR Padel through the Plugins screen.
  4. Go to Padel, add a match, enter the set scores, and paste the shortcode into any post or page.
sections.faq:
Does this work on its own?

No. SPOSCOR Padel requires the free SPOSCOR Core plugin, which provides the shared engine and settings.

How is a set decided?

Six games win a set with a two-game margin. At 6-6 the set is decided by a tie-break and recorded as 7-6. Best of three sets.

Can I run a league or tournament?

Yes, with the Pro plan, which adds unlimited tournaments, standings tables and knockout brackets.

What shortcodes are available?

[sposcor_scorecard id=”123″] shows the full match card. [sposcor_result id=”123″] shows a compact result. Tournament and standings shortcodes are available with Pro.
sections.changelog:
1.3.32

  • Fixed: on a live match, the sets-won dots were drawn three at a time in grey instead of two in the player’s colour.
  • Fixed: a match created from a tournament card no longer shows a made-up score such as 6-0 for each set. Only the sets won are carried over.
  • Added: plus and minus buttons on the score fields, saved as you press them.
  • Fixed: the FAQ said the free plan included one tournament, which it does not.
  • Fixed: the sets won were recalculated twice on the editing screen, which reset the result carried over from a tournament card to nil.
  • Fixed: on a narrow phone screen the scorecard header ran off the side. The logo now sits above the names so everything fits.
  • Changed: styles and scripts are now registered through WordPress instead of being written into the page.
  • Changed: a few translated labels are escaped on output, and Tested up to is declared only in the readme.
  • Requires SPOSCOR Core 1.1.13 or later.

1.3.28

  • Fixed: the 2-column match card layout spread into three or four columns on wide screens. It now stays at two columns, and still drops to one on narrow screens.

1.3.27

  • Fixed (Pro): tournament entries were lost on save.
  • Added (Pro): match cards now offer a dropdown to fill a pair straight from the entry list. Typing names by hand still works as before.

1.3.26

  • Added (Pro): tournament entries. Paste the pairs taking part straight from a spreadsheet, then pick them when filling in match cards instead of typing every name.

1.3.25

  • Maintenance release for deployment. Aligned the internal version number across the plugin header, version constant, sport config and readme.

1.3.24

  • Improved: Pro screens (tournament, standings, Pro design settings and OBS stream) are now translated into Japanese and Spanish (es_ES / es_AR). Unified the shared OBS main-card hook across sports. Scoreboard number size now defaults to 16px.

1.3.23

  • Pro design: the Highlight Body font-size setting now applies to the padel highlight list (previously ignored).
  • Pro design: hid options that don’t apply to padel (Player Name, Pitcher Record Player Name, Pitcher Record Row Background).

1.3.22

  • Plugin Check (WordPress.org) fixes: corrected the text domain to sposcor-padel across 40 strings, added translators comments to all placeholder strings, and escaped two outputs (the admin inline config script and the scorecard header). No functional changes.

1.3.21

  • Match main score: moved team logos to the inner side (next to the score) with player names on the outer side, matching the OBS overlay layout.

1.3.20

  • Removed the team logo from the front-end scoreboard table (players/sets only; the header logo is unchanged).
  • The compact result card ([sposcor_result]) now reflects the Pro design settings (colors, sizes, fonts).

1.3.19

  • OBS scoreboard player names are now larger and easier to read: both names on one line (slash-separated) with each player’s affiliation aligned directly beneath their name.

1.3.18

  • Enabled the OBS main-score renderer by adding the sposcor_obs_render_main hook to the shared OBS template (shared generation 1.11.1). The padel main view now shows full pairs, live game score, set dots and Set label. Other sports fall back to the existing main.

1.3.17

  • Added the OBS main-score renderer for padel (team logos, full pair names, live game score with tiebreak, set dots, Set label, series/venue, and no-logo handling). It activates once the shared OBS template exposes the sposcor_obs_render_main hook.

1.3.16

  • Scoreboard set dots now show the number of sets needed to win (2 for best-of-3) instead of the maximum number of sets, matching padel convention.

1.3.15

  • OBS scoreboard: removed the leading team logo (players/sets only).

1.3.14

  • OBS scoreboard polish: simplified to a single-colour scheme (theme text only, no gold/team colours) so it stays readable in Light mode, and tiebreak points now show larger in parentheses, e.g. 7(7).

1.3.13

  • OBS scoreboard now matches the front-end look: team logo, full pair names with affiliation, and Set 1/2/3 columns plus sets won (reuses the same renderers, styled for the transparent stream card).

1.3.12

  • OBS scoreboard: compact broadcast-style layout (pair name, tight set columns, sets-won) anchored bottom-left, instead of stretching across the full width.

1.3.11

  • OBS stream: the scoreboard view (?obs=1&sb=1) now renders a padel set-by-set table (games per set with tiebreaks, plus sets won) instead of the baseball inning table, on both the initial load and live updates.

1.3.10

  • Fix: creating a game from a tournament match card now carries the score over. Padel scores by sets, so the card’s sets are seeded into the game as won sets (6-0 placeholders) instead of being lost as 0-0; edit the game for the real per-set scores.
  • Added the OBS Stream URL box to the match editor for padel (Pro). It was registered but its file was missing, so the box never appeared.

1.3.9

  • Fix: the standings list is no longer wrapped in an extra container, so its width matches the rest of the page again (the minimal columns are unchanged).

1.3.8

  • Fix: the minimal standings columns from 1.3.7 now actually take effect (the scoped style is emitted inline so it renders reliably), so the list no longer shows the baseball columns or overflow the card.

1.3.7

  • Tournament standings (list view): padel now shows only the relevant columns (Pos, Team, W, L, Win%, Pts) and hides the baseball-style ones (G, D, GB, RS, RA). The matrix view is unchanged, and its cells still show the set-by-set detail.

1.3.6

  • Tournament standings matrix: cells for played games now show the set-by-set score under the result (e.g. 6(5)-4 / 3-6 / 7(7)-6(5)), matching the scoreboard. Each cell already links to the match detail page.

1.3.5

  • Fix: new tournament match cards no longer disappear on save when only the pair was entered (the pair now fills the underlying team name, so the card is kept and created games get a proper “A / B vs C / D” title).
  • Tournament editor: added a per-side “Show logo on scoreboard” toggle to the match card, saved to the card and to the game.

1.3.4

  • Tournament editor: the editable pair fields now appear on every match card, including new cards created before a game exists. The pair is stored on the card itself, so it persists without a game and is written to the game when you create one.

1.3.3

  • Fix: the editable pair fields in the tournament editor no longer disappear shortly after the page loads (they are re-applied if the match cards are re-rendered).

1.3.2

  • Tournament editor: for matches linked to a game, the match card now has editable pair fields (players and affiliation) in place of the generic Team Name / Abbr fields; edits are saved back to the game when the tournament is updated. The monogram logo option is hidden (padel uses emoji or image only).

1.3.1

  • Tournament match cards now honor each game’s “Show logo on scoreboard” setting, and no longer fall back to a monogram (padel uses emoji or image only).

1.3.0

  • Tournament match cards now use the same layout as the match scoreboard: each pair shows a logo, both player names stacked with their affiliation, per-set scores with tie-break points in parentheses, and the sets won.

1.2.5

  • Tournament match cards now show the pair’s players and their affiliation.

1.2.4

  • Tournament match cards now show the pair’s player names instead of a truncated abbreviation.

1.2.3

  • Tournament match cards now show tie-break points in parentheses, e.g. 6(5).

1.2.2

  • Tournament and league match cards now show the per-set game scores for padel.

1.2.1

  • Highlights now appears in the global settings section list even if settings were saved before the feature existed.

1.2.0

  • Restored the optional Powered by SPOSCOR credit on the compact result card.

1.1.9

  • Compact result shortcode now shows the same padel header (players, logos, dots, tie-break) plus a View Details link.

1.1.8

  • Internal: header rendering extracted into a reusable set-type function (no visible change).

1.1.7

  • More robust live Sets recalculation in the editor (direct input listeners, runs on load).

1.1.6

  • The Sets column in the editor now updates live as you type set scores, matching the other sports.

1.1.5

  • Added optional tie-break points: enter per set in admin, shown as 6(5) in the scorecard and (5-4) in the live header. Display only, no effect on set totals.

1.1.4

  • The global settings section list now includes newly added sections such as highlights.

1.1.3

  • Highlights now appear for existing matches whose saved section order predated the feature.

1.1.2

  • Added padel highlights: log point moments (set, point score, pair) from dropdowns; shown under the scoreboard and updated live.

1.1.1

  • Pulled logos and names toward the center score; scoreboard column relabeled Players.

1.1.0

  • Live header now updates the current-set games, set number and won-set dots on refresh (via a shared engine live state). Fixed logo alignment and the show-logo checkbox display.

1.0.9

  • Emoji presets tuned for padel (added ball and paddle icons, removed baseball).

1.0.8

  • New live-style header: logos outside, large player names with affiliation, current set games with set number and won-set dots.

1.0.7

  • Fixed the show-logo checkbox toggling erratically.

1.0.6

  • Logo and color now sit side by side in the editor.

1.0.5

  • Team color is now its own block beside the logo; header logo respects the per-pair show/hide toggle.

1.0.4

  • Moved team color beside the logo label; logo now hidden by default per pair.

1.0.3

  • Fixed pair headings (Pair 1 / Pair 2); players shown first; team color moved beside the logo.

1.0.2

  • Renamed Team Settings to Player Settings; input is now players and affiliation.
  • Removed team name, short name and monogram; logo is emoji or image only, with a per-team show/hide toggle.

1.0.1

  • Added player names and affiliation for each pair (doubles).
  • Fixed the tournament post type identifier.

1.0.0

  • Initial release of SPOSCOR Padel.
  • Set-by-set scoreboard (best of 3, six games, two-game margin, tie-break).
  • Doubles pairs with team colors and logos.
  • Shared tournament, settings, and OBS streaming layers (Pro).
  • Compatible with WordPress 7.1.
